# 結論（先に）

これは Borel 版ではなく、全体の $O(SL_2)$ に対する古典 $q=1$ の結果で
ある。$\mathfrak m=(b,c,\xi)$ とし、$f\equiv_N g$ を
$f-g\in\mathfrak m^{N+1}$ の意味に書く。この記法で、今回得られた
有限次数 dual basis approximation は次の通り。

$$
\begin{aligned}
E^\vee_{\le 2}&\equiv_2 b+b\xi,\\
F^\vee_{\le 2}&\equiv_2 c-c\xi,\\
H^\vee_{\le 2}&\equiv_2 \xi-bc-\frac12\xi^2;
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
E^\vee_{\le 3}&\equiv_3 b+b\xi-b^2c,\\
F^\vee_{\le 3}&\equiv_3 c-c\xi+bc^2+c\xi^2,\\
H^\vee_{\le 3}&\equiv_3 \xi-bc-\frac12\xi^2+\frac13\xi^3;
\end{aligned}
$$

そして degree 4 まで計算すると、

$$
\begin{aligned}
E^\vee_{\le 4}&\equiv_4 b+b\xi-b^2c-b^2c\xi,\\
F^\vee_{\le 4}&\equiv_4 c-c\xi+bc^2+c\xi^2-c\xi^3-bc^2\xi,\\
H^\vee_{\le 4}&\equiv_4 \xi-bc-\frac12\xi^2+\frac13\xi^3
 -\frac14\xi^4+\frac12b^2c^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

ここから得られる閉形式は

$$
E^\vee=\frac{b}{d},\qquad
F^\vee=cd,\qquad
H^\vee=-\log d,
$$

すなわち $\xi=a-1,\ \eta=bc$ を使えば

$$
E^\vee=\frac{1+\xi}{1+\eta}b,\qquad
F^\vee=\frac{1+\eta}{1+\xi}c,\qquad
H^\vee=\log(1+\xi)-\log(1+\eta).
$$

一般の PBW monomial に対する dual basis は、$i,j,k\ge0$ に対して

$$
\boxed{
\bigl(E^iF^jH^k\bigr)^\vee
=\frac1{i!\,j!\,k!}
\left(\frac bd\right)^i(cd)^j(-\log d)^k
}
$$

である。上に掲げた degree 2--4 の式は、この閉形式を
$\mathfrak m=(b,c,\xi)$ の次数で展開したものにほかならない。以下で、
この一般式を PBW 順序と右不変ベクトル場を用いて証明し、最後に QMD の
厳密有理数計算で degree 6 まで展開を照合する。

# Scope

This notebook ports the **full** `sl2_dualbasis.mlx` experiment, not the
Borel-only calculation.  The source MATLAB Live Script is:

```text
lib/algebra/Execution/SLnDual/sl2_dualbasis.mlx
```

The source document is titled
$U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\leftrightarrow F_q(SL_2)$ duality, but the calculation
implemented there uses `Usl2Full` and `FSL2Full` at the classical value
$q=1$.  This QMD records that same classical finite-degree experiment.

We use the coordinate chart

$$
\xi=a-1,\qquad \eta=bc,
\qquad d=\frac{1+bc}{1+\xi},
$$

where the last equality is expanded as a formal power series and truncated at
the requested degree.  The coordinate algebra relation is
$ad-bc=1$.

The target is a filtered approximation to the three functionals dual to
$E,F,H$:

$$
\langle E^\vee,E\rangle=\langle F^\vee,F\rangle
=\langle H^\vee,H\rangle=1,
\qquad
\langle X^\vee,Y\rangle=0\quad(X\ne Y),
$$

with every candidate orthogonal to the PBW monomials of degrees $2$ through
the current cutoff.

# Exact truncated coordinate algebra

The following small implementation is intentionally local to the notebook.
It uses only Julia built-ins and `Rational{BigInt}` coefficients, so the
calculation does not hide a floating-point or CAS dependency.

```{julia}
using LinearAlgebra

const Monomial = NTuple{3,Int}
const Rat = Rational{BigInt}
const ZERO_MONOMIAL = (0, 0, 0)

asrat(x::Rat) = x
asrat(x::Integer) = BigInt(x) // BigInt(1)
asrat(x::Rational) = BigInt(numerator(x)) // BigInt(denominator(x))

struct Poly
    terms::Dict{Monomial,Rat}
end

Poly() = Poly(Dict{Monomial,Rat}())

function monomial(exponents::Monomial, coefficient=one(Rat))
    c = asrat(coefficient)
    c == 0 && return Poly()
    Poly(Dict(exponents => c))
end

function add_term!(terms::Dict{K,Rat}, exponent::K,
                   coefficient::Rat) where {K}
    coefficient == 0 && return terms
    value = get(terms, exponent, zero(Rat)) + coefficient
    if value == 0
        delete!(terms, exponent)
    else
        terms[exponent] = value
    end
    return terms
end

function Base.:+(p::Poly, q::Poly)
    terms = copy(p.terms)
    for (e, c) in q.terms
        add_term!(terms, e, c)
    end
    Poly(terms)
end

Base.:-(p::Poly) = Poly(Dict(e => -c for (e, c) in p.terms))
Base.:-(p::Poly, q::Poly) = p + (-q)

Base.:(==)(p::Poly, q::Poly) = p.terms == q.terms

function Base.:*(p::Poly, q::Poly)
    terms = Dict{Monomial,Rat}()
    for (ep, cp) in p.terms, (eq, cq) in q.terms
        exponent = ntuple(i -> ep[i] + eq[i], 3)
        add_term!(terms, exponent, cp * cq)
    end
    Poly(terms)
end

Base.:*(c::Integer, p::Poly) = asrat(c) * p
Base.:*(p::Poly, c::Integer) = c * p
Base.:*(c::Rational, p::Poly) = Poly(Dict(e => asrat(c) * v for (e, v) in p.terms))
Base.:*(p::Poly, c::Rational) = c * p

function Base.:^(p::Poly, n::Integer)
    n < 0 && throw(ArgumentError("negative polynomial powers are not supported"))
    result = monomial(ZERO_MONOMIAL)
    for _ in 1:n
        result = result * p
    end
    result
end

function truncate_poly(p::Poly, degree::Int)
    Poly(Dict(e => c for (e, c) in p.terms if sum(e) <= degree))
end

constant_term(p::Poly) = get(p.terms, ZERO_MONOMIAL, zero(Rat))

const ONE_POLY = monomial(ZERO_MONOMIAL)
const B = monomial((1, 0, 0))
const C = monomial((0, 1, 0))
const XI = monomial((0, 0, 1))
const A = ONE_POLY + XI

function coordinate_monomials(degree::Int)
    [monomial((i, j, degree - i - j))
     for i in 0:degree for j in 0:(degree - i)]
end

function exponent_compositions(degree::Int)
    [(i, j, degree - i - j)
     for i in 0:degree for j in 0:(degree - i)]
end
```

For the full coordinate algebra, the coproducts needed in the source
experiment are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta(b)&=a\otimes b+b\otimes d,\\
\Delta(c)&=c\otimes a+d\otimes c,\\
\Delta(\xi)&=a\otimes a+b\otimes c-1\otimes1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The formal expansion of $d$ is truncated before it enters the coproduct.

```{julia}
const TensorMonomial = Tuple{Monomial,Monomial}

struct TensorPoly
    terms::Dict{TensorMonomial,Rat}
end

TensorPoly() = TensorPoly(Dict{TensorMonomial,Rat}())

tensor_product(p::Poly, q::Poly) = TensorPoly(
    Dict((ep, eq) => cp * cq
         for (ep, cp) in p.terms for (eq, cq) in q.terms))

tensor_one() = tensor_product(ONE_POLY, ONE_POLY)

function Base.:+(p::TensorPoly, q::TensorPoly)
    terms = copy(p.terms)
    for (e, c) in q.terms
        value = get(terms, e, zero(Rat)) + c
        if value == 0
            delete!(terms, e)
        else
            terms[e] = value
        end
    end
    TensorPoly(terms)
end

Base.:-(p::TensorPoly) = TensorPoly(Dict(e => -c for (e, c) in p.terms))
Base.:-(p::TensorPoly, q::TensorPoly) = p + (-q)

function tensor_scale(c::Rat, p::TensorPoly)
    TensorPoly(Dict(e => c * v for (e, v) in p.terms if c * v != 0))
end

function tensor_mul(p::TensorPoly, q::TensorPoly, degree::Int)
    terms = Dict{TensorMonomial,Rat}()
    for ((elp, erp), cp) in p.terms, ((elq, erq), cq) in q.terms
        left = ntuple(i -> elp[i] + elq[i], 3)
        right = ntuple(i -> erp[i] + erq[i], 3)
        if sum(left) <= degree && sum(right) <= degree
            key = (left, right)
            add_term!(terms, key, cp * cq)
        end
    end
    TensorPoly(terms)
end

mutable struct PairingContext
    degree::Int
    delta_generators::Vector{TensorPoly}
    delta_cache::Dict{Monomial,TensorPoly}
    pairing_cache::Dict{Any,Rat}
end

function formal_d(degree::Int)
    inverse_a = Poly()
    for k in 0:degree
        inverse_a += ((-1)^k) * (XI^k)
    end
    truncate_poly((ONE_POLY + B * C) * inverse_a, degree)
end

function PairingContext(degree::Int)
    d = formal_d(degree)
    delta_b = tensor_product(A, B) + tensor_product(B, d)
    delta_c = tensor_product(C, A) + tensor_product(d, C)
    delta_xi = tensor_product(A, A) + tensor_product(B, C) - tensor_one()
    PairingContext(degree, [delta_b, delta_c, delta_xi],
                   Dict{Monomial,TensorPoly}(), Dict{Any,Rat}())
end

function delta_monomial(ctx::PairingContext, exponent::Monomial)
    haskey(ctx.delta_cache, exponent) && return ctx.delta_cache[exponent]
    result = tensor_one()
    for variable in 1:3
        for _ in 1:exponent[variable]
            result = tensor_mul(result, ctx.delta_generators[variable], ctx.degree)
        end
    end
    ctx.delta_cache[exponent] = result
    result
end

function delta_poly(ctx::PairingContext, p::Poly)
    result = TensorPoly()
    for (exponent, coefficient) in p.terms
        result = result + tensor_scale(coefficient,
                                       delta_monomial(ctx, exponent))
    end
    result
end

function base_pair(coordinate_variable::Int, enveloping_generator::Int)
    # (b,c,xi) paired with (E,F,H), respectively.
    (coordinate_variable == enveloping_generator) ? one(Rat) : zero(Rat)
end

function pair_monomial(ctx::PairingContext, exponent::Monomial,
                       word::Tuple)
    key = (exponent, word)
    haskey(ctx.pairing_cache, key) && return ctx.pairing_cache[key]

    result = if isempty(word)
        exponent == ZERO_MONOMIAL ? one(Rat) : zero(Rat)
    elseif length(word) == 1
        # E,F,H are primitive.  Since b,c,xi all have zero counit, a
        # coordinate monomial of degree > 1 pairs trivially with one generator.
        total_degree = sum(exponent)
        if total_degree == 0
            zero(Rat)
        elseif total_degree == 1
            coordinate_variable = findfirst(>(0), exponent)
            base_pair(coordinate_variable, word[1])
        else
            zero(Rat)
        end
    else
        first_generator = word[1]
        remaining_word = Tuple(word[2:end])
        value = zero(Rat)
        for ((left_exponent, right_exponent), coefficient) in
            delta_monomial(ctx, exponent).terms
            left = monomial(left_exponent)
            right = monomial(right_exponent)
            value += coefficient *
                pair_poly_word(ctx, left, (first_generator,)) *
                pair_poly_word(ctx, right, remaining_word)
        end
        value
    end

    ctx.pairing_cache[key] = result
    result
end

function pair_poly_word(ctx::PairingContext, p::Poly, word::Tuple)
    sum(coefficient * pair_monomial(ctx, exponent, word)
        for (exponent, coefficient) in p.terms; init=zero(Rat))
end
```

The chart relation and the generator pairing matrix agree with the MATLAB
classes (`FSL2Full.HPGen`) at the requested truncation.

```{julia}
cutoff = 6
ctx = PairingContext(cutoff)
d = formal_d(cutoff)

# The relation is exact modulo terms above the cutoff.
test_relation = truncate_poly(A * d - B * C - ONE_POLY, cutoff)
@assert isempty(test_relation.terms)

# Recover the source generator pairings for a,b,c,d,xi,d-1.
coordinate_generators = [A, B, C, d, XI, d - ONE_POLY]
generator_pairing = [
    pair_poly_word(ctx, f, (u,)) for f in coordinate_generators for u in 1:3
]
generator_pairing = reshape(generator_pairing, 3, 6)'

println("generator pairing rows = [a b c d xi d-1]")
println(generator_pairing)
@assert generator_pairing == Rat[
    0 0 1;
    1 0 0;
    0 1 0;
    0 0 -1;
    0 0 1;
    0 0 -1
]
```

# 数学的証明：有限次数 dual basis の存在と一意性

## 設定

$G=SL_2$ の単位元近傍の形式局所環を

$$
R=\mathbb{Q}[[b,c,\xi]],\qquad \xi=a-1,
\qquad d=\frac{1+bc}{1+\xi}
$$

とする。$R$ の次数 filtration は
$\mathfrak m=(b,c,\xi)$ によって定め、$R_{>N}=\mathfrak m^{N+1}$ と書く。
古典 Hopf pairing は、生成元について

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 & E&F&H\\ \hline
b&1&0&0\\
c&0&1&0\\
\xi&0&0&1
\end{array}
$$

とし、

$$
\langle fg,u\rangle
=\langle f\otimes g,\Delta_U(u)\rangle,
\qquad
\langle f,uv\rangle
=\langle\Delta_R(f),u\otimes v\rangle
$$

で拡張する。ここで $E,F,H$ は primitive、すなわち
$\Delta_U(X)=X\otimes1+1\otimes X$ である。$R$ 側の coproduct は

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_R(b)&=a\otimes b+b\otimes d,\\
\Delta_R(c)&=c\otimes a+d\otimes c,\\
\Delta_R(\xi)&=a\otimes a+b\otimes c-1\otimes1.
\end{aligned}
$$

これは $m_{ij}\mapsto\sum_km_{ik}\otimes m_{kj}$ と
$\xi=a-1$ から直接従う。

## 補題（各次数の pairing 行列は可逆）

$R_r=\mathfrak m^r/\mathfrak m^{r+1}$ の monomial basis を
$b^pc^q\xi^s$（$p+q+s=r$）とし、$U_r$ の PBW basis を
$E^iF^jH^k$（$i+j+k=r$）とする。この二つの間の pairing 行列

$$
P_r=\bigl(\langle b^pc^q\xi^s,E^iF^jH^k\rangle\bigr)
$$

は可逆である。

### 証明

右不変ベクトル場を $R_E,R_F,R_H$ と書く。単位元での一次部分は、
生成元 pairing の表そのものから

$$
R_E=\partial_b+O(\mathfrak m),\qquad
R_F=\partial_c+O(\mathfrak m),\qquad
R_H=\partial_\xi+O(\mathfrak m)
$$

となる。したがって PBW monomial $E^iF^jH^k$ が単位元で作用する
principal part は

$$
\partial_b^i\partial_c^j\partial_\xi^k
$$

であり、同じ次数の coordinate monomial に作用させた主係数は
$i!j!k!$ である。$O(\mathfrak m)$ の係数から来る項は filtration を
一段以上下げるだけなので、monomial order を degree 降順に取ると
$P_r$ は対角成分 $i!j!k!\ne0$ を持つ triangular matrix になる。
よって $P_r$ は可逆である。∎

## 命題（cutoff dual basis の存在・一意性）

各 $N\ge1$ に対し、$D_E^{(N)},D_F^{(N)},D_H^{(N)}\in R/R_{>N}$ で

$$
\langle D_X^{(N)},Y\rangle=\delta_{X,Y},
\qquad
\langle D_X^{(N)},E^iF^jH^k\rangle=0
$$

$2\le i+j+k\le N$ を満たすものが一意に存在する。

### 証明

$N-1$ 次で条件を満たす $D_X^{(N-1)}$ が得られているとする。次数 $N$
の補正を

$$
D_X^{(N)}=D_X^{(N-1)}
 +\sum_{p+q+s=N}x^{(X)}_{p,q,s}b^pc^q\xi^s
$$

と置く。右不変微分作用素の order より、次数 $N$ の coordinate term は
次数 $<N$ の PBW monomial との pairing に寄与しない。したがって新しい
未知係数は次数 $N$ の条件だけに現れ、条件式は

$$
P_N\,x^{(X)}=-v^{(X)},
$$

という線形方程式になる。ここで $v^{(X)}$ は既知の
$D_X^{(N-1)}$ の次数 $N$ PBW monomial に対する pairing 値である。
補題により $P_N$ は可逆なので、$x^{(X)}$ は一意に決まる。次数 1 の
初期値 $D_E^{(1)}=b,D_F^{(1)}=c,D_H^{(1)}=\xi$ から帰納すれば、
任意の有限 cutoff に対する存在と一意性が従う。∎

## 今回の係数への適用

上の命題を $N=2,3,4$ に適用し、coproduct を展開すると、先頭の結論に
掲げた係数が得られる。例えば degree 2 の未知補正を

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_E^{(2)}&=b+\sum_{p+q+s=2}x^{(E)}_{p,q,s}b^pc^q\xi^s,\\
D_F^{(2)}&=c+\sum_{p+q+s=2}x^{(F)}_{p,q,s}b^pc^q\xi^s,\\
D_H^{(2)}&=\xi+\sum_{p+q+s=2}x^{(H)}_{p,q,s}b^pc^q\xi^s
\end{aligned}
$$

と置くと、$P_2x^{(X)}=-v^{(X)}$ の解はそれぞれ

$$
\begin{aligned}
x^{(E)}&=b\xi,\\
x^{(F)}&=-c\xi,\\
x^{(H)}&=-bc-\frac12\xi^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

degree 2 の cancellation は、例えば次の four pairings によって見える。

$$
\begin{array}{c|cc}
\text{condition}&\text{old term}&\text{new term}\\ \hline
\langle\,\cdot\,,EH\rangle\text{ for }D_E
    &\langle b,EH\rangle=-1&\langle b\xi,EH\rangle=1\\
\langle\,\cdot\,,FH\rangle\text{ for }D_F
    &\langle c,FH\rangle=1&\langle c\xi,FH\rangle=1\\
\langle\,\cdot\,,EF\rangle\text{ for }D_H
    &\langle\xi,EF\rangle=1&\langle bc,EF\rangle=1\\
\langle\,\cdot\,,H^2\rangle\text{ for }D_H
    &\langle\xi,H^2\rangle=1&\langle\xi^2,H^2\rangle=2
\end{array}
$$

従って $b+b\xi$、$c-c\xi$、
$\xi-bc-\frac12\xi^2$ でそれぞれの defect が消える。他の degree 2
PBW monomial に対する defect は同じ coproduct recursion で 0 になり、
degree 3, 4 ではこの手続きを各次数の全 monomial に対して繰り返す。

degree 3, 4 でも同じ一意決定を繰り返す。QMD の
`solve_exact` はこの $P_Nx=-v$ を有理数上で実行しており、最後の
`@assert` は各 $N\le\texttt{cutoff}$ の pairing 条件を全 PBW monomial について確認する。

この有限次数の帰納法は、以下の閉形式を次数ごとに復元する計算法として
理解できる。

## 命題（一般 PBW dual basis の閉形式）

形式座標

$$
 x=\frac bd,\qquad y=cd,\qquad z=-\log d
$$

を置く。このとき、任意の $i,j,k\ge0$ に対し

$$
\boxed{
\bigl(E^iF^jH^k\bigr)^\vee
=\frac{x^iy^jz^k}{i!j!k!}
=\frac1{i!j!k!}
\left(\frac bd\right)^i(cd)^j(-\log d)^k
}
$$

である。

### 証明

単位元近傍では $d$ は可逆なので、$(x,y,z)$ を形式局所座標として
使える。逆変換は

$$
 d=e^{-z},\qquad b=xe^{-z},\qquad c=ye^z,
\qquad a=(1+xy)e^z
$$

である。$g=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ に右から
$\exp(tE),\exp(tF),\exp(tH)$ を掛けて微分すると、右不変ベクトル場は

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_E&=e^{2z}\bigl(\partial_x+y^2\partial_y-y\partial_z\bigr),\\
R_F&=e^{-2z}\partial_y,\\
R_H&=\partial_z.
\end{aligned}
$$

Pairing の定義より

$$
\langle f,E^iF^jH^k\rangle
=\bigl(R_E^iR_F^jR_H^k f\bigr)(0,0,0).
$$

ここで右辺の作用は右端の $R_H^k$ から始まる。まず $R_H^k$
は $z^r$ を $r!/(r-k)!\,z^{r-k}$ に写す。次に $R_F^j$ は
$y^q$ を $q!/(q-j)!\,y^{q-j}$ に写す。最後に $R_E$ のうち
$\partial_x$ 以外の項は必ず $y$ 因子を作るため、単位元での値に
寄与しない。従って $x^py^qz^r$ に対しては

$$
\bigl(R_E^iR_F^jR_H^k x^py^qz^r\bigr)(0,0,0)
=p!q!r!\,\delta_{i,p}\delta_{j,q}\delta_{k,r}.
$$

よって $x^iy^jz^k/(i!j!k!)$ は PBW monomial
$E^iF^jH^k$ に 1 を与え、他の PBW monomial に 0 を与える。PBW 定理
によりこれらが全 basis を成すので、表示された式が dual basis である。∎

この命題の $i,j,k$ を 1 つずつ選べば、生成元の dual
$E^\vee=x,F^\vee=y,H^\vee=z$ が得られる。一般の dual basis は、
まさにその積を $i!j!k!$ で割ったものになっている。

# Degree-by-degree dual-basis construction

The source `.mlx` solves a symbolic system for each degree.  Here the same
system is triangularized explicitly.  At degree $r$, the unknown correction
has one coefficient for each degree-$r$ monomial in $(b,c,\xi)$, and the
conditions are its pairings with all degree-$r$ PBW monomials
$E^iF^jH^k$.

```{julia}
function enveloping_word(exponent::Monomial)
    i, j, k = exponent
    Tuple(vcat(fill(1, i), fill(2, j), fill(3, k)))
end

enveloping_words(degree::Int) =
    [enveloping_word(e) for e in exponent_compositions(degree)]

function solve_exact(A::Matrix{Rat}, rhs::Vector{Rat})
    n, m = size(A)
    n == m || throw(DimensionMismatch("expected a square exact system"))
    augmented = hcat(copy(A), reshape(copy(rhs), n, 1))

    for column in 1:n
        pivot = findfirst(row -> augmented[row, column] != 0, column:n)
        pivot === nothing && error("singular exact system at column $column")
        pivot += column - 1
        if pivot != column
            augmented[[column, pivot], :] = augmented[[pivot, column], :]
        end
        augmented[column, :] ./= augmented[column, column]
        for row in 1:n
            row == column && continue
            factor = augmented[row, column]
            factor == 0 && continue
            augmented[row, :] .-= factor .* augmented[column, :]
        end
    end
    augmented[:, n + 1]
end

function add_correction(previous::Poly, monomials::Vector{Poly},
                        coefficients::Vector{Rat})
    correction = Poly()
    for (coefficient, monomial_term) in zip(coefficients, monomials)
        correction += coefficient * monomial_term
    end
    previous + correction
end

function solve_next_degree(ctx::PairingContext, previous::Vector{Poly},
                           degree::Int)
    coordinate_basis = coordinate_monomials(degree)
    enveloping_basis = enveloping_words(degree)
    matrix = Rat[
        pair_poly_word(ctx, coordinate_basis[column], enveloping_basis[row])
        for row in eachindex(enveloping_basis), column in eachindex(coordinate_basis)
    ]

    @assert size(matrix) == (length(enveloping_basis), length(coordinate_basis))
    @assert size(matrix, 1) == size(matrix, 2)

    next_duals = Poly[]
    for target in previous
        rhs = Rat[-pair_poly_word(ctx, target, word)
                  for word in enveloping_basis]
        coefficients = solve_exact(matrix, rhs)
        push!(next_duals, add_correction(target, coordinate_basis, coefficients))
    end
    next_duals
end

function format_rational(value::Rat)
    value == 0 && return "0"
    denominator(value) == 1 ? string(numerator(value)) :
        string(numerator(value), "/", denominator(value))
end

function coordinate_factor(exponent::Monomial)
    names = ("b", "c", "\\xi")
    factors = String[]
    for (name, power) in zip(names, exponent)
        power == 0 && continue
        push!(factors, power == 1 ? name : "$name^{$power}")
    end
    isempty(factors) ? "1" : join(factors, " ")
end

function format_poly(p::Poly)
    entries = collect(p.terms)
    sort!(entries; by = x -> (sum(x[1]), x[1]))
    isempty(entries) && return "0"
    chunks = String[]
    for (exponent, coefficient) in entries
        sign = coefficient < 0 ? "-" : "+"
        magnitude = abs(coefficient)
        factor = coordinate_factor(exponent)
        body = magnitude == 1 && factor != "1" ? factor :
            (factor == "1" ? format_rational(magnitude) :
             "$(format_rational(magnitude)) $factor")
        if isempty(chunks)
            push!(chunks, coefficient < 0 ? "-$body" : body)
        else
            push!(chunks, "$sign $body")
        end
    end
    join(chunks, " ")
end

base_duals = [B, C, XI]
duals_by_degree = Dict{Int,Vector{Poly}}(1 => base_duals)
for degree in 2:cutoff
    duals_by_degree[degree] = solve_next_degree(ctx, duals_by_degree[degree - 1], degree)
end

for degree in 1:cutoff
    println("degree $degree")
    for (label, dual) in zip(("E", "F", "H"), duals_by_degree[degree])
        println("  $label^vee = $(format_poly(dual))")
    end
end
```

The first two nontrivial degrees reproduce the source experiment:

```{julia}
expected_degree_2 = [
    B + B * XI,
    C - C * XI,
    XI - B * C - (1 // 2) * (XI^2),
]

expected_degree_3 = [
    B + B * XI - (B^2) * C,
    C - C * XI + B * (C^2) + C * (XI^2),
    XI - B * C - (1 // 2) * (XI^2) + (1 // 3) * (XI^3),
]

@assert duals_by_degree[2] == expected_degree_2
@assert duals_by_degree[3] == expected_degree_3

println("degree-2 and degree-3 formulas match the saved MATLAB result")
```

The closed formula can also be expanded directly and compared with the
degree-by-degree solver.  The next cell performs that comparison through the
current cutoff and then checks the full PBW duality table in the same finite
jet.

```{julia}
function closed_form_generators(degree::Int)
    inverse_eta = Poly()
    inverse_a = Poly()
    for k in 0:degree
        inverse_eta += (-1)^k * ((B * C)^k)
        inverse_a += (-1)^k * (XI^k)
    end

    x = truncate_poly(B * A * inverse_eta, degree)
    y = truncate_poly(C * (ONE_POLY + B * C) * inverse_a, degree)

    z = Poly()
    for k in 1:degree
        coefficient = asrat((-1)^(k + 1)) / asrat(k)
        z += coefficient * (XI^k - (B * C)^k)
    end
    [x, y, truncate_poly(z, degree)]
end

for degree in 1:cutoff
    @assert duals_by_degree[degree] == closed_form_generators(degree)
end
println("closed generator formula matches through degree $cutoff")

function closed_basis_element(exponent::Monomial, degree::Int)
    i, j, k = exponent
    x, y, z = closed_form_generators(degree)
    scale = one(Rat) /
        (asrat(factorial(i)) * asrat(factorial(j)) * asrat(factorial(k)))
    truncate_poly(scale * (x^i) * (y^j) * (z^k), degree)
end

all_exponents = [exponent for degree in 0:cutoff
                 for exponent in exponent_compositions(degree)]
all_words = [enveloping_word(exponent) for exponent in all_exponents]

for (target_exponent, target_element) in
    zip(all_exponents, [closed_basis_element(e, cutoff) for e in all_exponents])
    for (source_exponent, source_word) in zip(all_exponents, all_words)
        value = pair_poly_word(ctx, target_element, source_word)
        expected = target_exponent == source_exponent ? one(Rat) : zero(Rat)
        @assert value == expected
    end
end
println("full PBW duality table verified through degree $cutoff")
```

# Verification at the finite scope

The following checks are the executable finite-jet certificate for the closed
formula proved above.  They verify the exact rational identities through the
stated cutoff.

```{julia}
function check_duality(ctx::PairingContext, duals::Vector{Poly},
                       cutoff_degree::Int)
    # Linear normalization and cross-pairing.
    linear_words = [(1,), (2,), (3,)]
    linear_matrix = Rat[
        pair_poly_word(ctx, duals[row], linear_words[column])
        for row in 1:3, column in 1:3
    ]
    @assert linear_matrix == Matrix{Rat}(I, 3, 3)

    residual_counts = Dict{Int,Int}()
    for degree in 2:cutoff_degree
        words = enveloping_words(degree)
        residuals = [pair_poly_word(ctx, dual, word)
                     for dual in duals for word in words]
        residual_counts[degree] = count(!iszero, residuals)
        @assert all(iszero, residuals)
    end
    (linear_matrix=linear_matrix,
     residual_counts=[residual_counts[degree] for degree in 2:cutoff_degree])
end

verification = Dict{Int,Any}()
for degree in 1:cutoff
    verification[degree] = check_duality(ctx, duals_by_degree[degree], degree)
end

println("verified cutoffs = ", sort(collect(keys(verification))))
for degree in 1:cutoff
    println("  degree $degree: ", verification[degree])
end
```

# Interpretation and boundary

At the exact finite scope `cutoff = 6`, the Julia port verifies:

- the full `SL2` coordinate chart relation $ad-bc=1$ modulo discarded terms;
- the source generator pairing matrix;
- the degree-2 and degree-3 formulas saved in `sl2_dualbasis.mlx`;
- the closed generator formula through degree 6;
- the full PBW duality table through degree 6.

The right-invariant-vector-field argument above proves the closed formula in
the completed classical coordinate ring.  The QMD execution is the exact
finite-jet certificate through cutoff 6.  This remains the classical
$q=1$ calculation; the quantum ($q\ne1$) version requires replacing the
primitive coproducts and the classical coordinate coproduct by fixed
$U_q(sl_2)$ and $O_q(SL_2)$ conventions.
